diagnosis.root_cause: The EPON0/7 PON is saturating during evening demand. Current traffic is 912 Mbps with a 948 Mbps peak on the shared PON, explaining the customer's evening slowdown despite healthy optical, authentication, VLAN, router, and OLT state.
evidence: The customer's current RX power is -21.27 dBm and TX power is 2.37 dBm, both within normal ranges.
Seven-day RX telemetry remains stable around -21 dBm with no decline into degraded range; TX power, TX bias current, and distance are also stable, ruling out fibre, laser, and distance faults.
All tested peers on EPON0/7 are online and responding, and the OLT ping, SNMP, and ONU subtree all respond normally; this rules out ONU, splitter, PON-port, and OLT failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy and OLT CPU, memory, and temperature are not abnormally loaded.
The customer has 2 sessions in 24 hours with an average duration of 711 minutes, which is normal and not session flapping.
RADIUS records are present and consistent with CRM, and the actual customer VLAN is 1017 as expected; authentication and provisioning are therefore not the cause.
EPON0/7 is carrying 912 Mbps currently, with a 948 Mbps peak versus a 488 Mbps average, indicating near-capacity shared-PON utilization consistent with an evening-only slowdown.
Because the capacity issue is on the shared PON rather than solely on the customer's ONU, the affected scope is pon_port.

remediation.action: Review evening utilization and per-ONU traffic on EPON0/7, then relieve the shared capacity constraint by moving customers to another PON, splitting or upgrading the access segment, or applying appropriate capacity/QoS controls. Continue monitoring peak utilization and customer throughput after remediation.

ground_truth.root_cause: EPON0/7 carries 47 customers and its evening load is reaching 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average, close to the port's shared capacity ceiling. Throughput degrades for everyone on the port during peak hours. No optical or authentication fault exists.
expected_reasoning: The complaint is time-of-day specific, which points at load rather than at a physical fault
RX is flat at -21.2 dBm inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe shows every ONU on the port online with normal optical readings
RADIUS is clean and sessions are long and stable, so authentication is not involved
PON port traffic is at 912 Mbps against a 488 Mbps average
Daily traffic for this customer is roughly three times the network mean and rising, not falling
Every fault-driven degradation reduces traffic; congestion raises it, so the direction is the discriminator
The customer's own throughput series drops sharply during the same evening hours each day
The port carries 47 customers, at the top of the observed occupancy distribution
This is capacity exhaustion on a shared port, not a fault on any one line

expected_escalation.review_reason: EPON0/7 needs a capacity review; 47 customers on one port with evening load near ceiling

distractors: Multi-customer slowness resembles a splitter or feeder degradation
Elevated OLT CPU and temperature could be read as device stress causing the slowness
Reduced throughput in the speed series looks like a link problem
